title: The Potter's Empire
tagline: He made china fashionable, pottery industrial, and beauty accessible to all.

scenes.text: Staffordshire, England, 1760s. Josiah Wedgwood hobbles through his pottery on a peg leg — a childhood illness cost him his right knee — testing glaze after glaze. He has conducted ten thousand experiments. He is building something the world has never seen: an industrial pottery empire.

scenes.speaker: Josiah Wedgwood
scenes.text: If Queen Charlotte uses our cream-colored earthenware, every household in England will want a set. I will call it Queen's Ware. We do not merely make pots — we manufacture desire.

challenge.instruction: Queen Charlotte's order has made Wedgwood's cream-coloured ware the fashion. Carry the stack of dishes to the packing bench one at a time, never a larger on a smaller — a single broken piece shames the 'Potter to Her Majesty'.
challenge.fact: Josiah Wedgwood didn't just make pottery — he invented modern manufacturing. He introduced quality control, a money-back guarantee, free delivery, and celebrity endorsements. His factory pioneered the division of labour decades before Adam Smith wrote about it.

scenes.text: Wedgwood invented modern marketing: he opened the first showroom in London, sent catalogs to customers across Europe, offered free returns, and used celebrity endorsements from royalty. He was also an obsessive experimentalist — his laboratory notebooks record thousands of chemical trials in the search for the perfect Jasperware blue.

scenes.speaker: Business Partner
scenes.text: Josiah, why do you work so hard on this anti-slavery medallion? It will not sell like tableware. You could spend that energy on more profitable things.

challenge.instruction: Thousands of trials, and the jasper still comes out wrong. Stain the white body with oxides until it matches the pale blue Wedgwood is after.
challenge.fact: Wedgwood spent years and thousands of experiments to develop Jasperware — a ceramic so consistent that every piece looked identical. He believed in what today we call quality control: testing every batch, recording every failure. His laboratory notebooks survive, filled with meticulous records of clay, glaze, and kiln temperature.

scenes.speaker: Josiah Wedgwood
scenes.text: Some things are more important than profit. 'Am I Not a Man and a Brother?' — these words, around an image of a kneeling slave, will be worn as a brooch, carried as a token, shown to members of Parliament. Art can be an argument. Beauty can carry a demand for justice.

challenge.instruction: The medallions go out by the thousand, and Wedgwood's canal company now brings in limestone on rails from Caldon Low. Sort the wagons at Froghall onto the sidings and send them out to the boats in order.
challenge.fact: Charles Darwin was Josiah Wedgwood's grandson — his mother Susannah was Wedgwood's daughter, and his wife Emma was Wedgwood's granddaughter. Darwin married his own cousin from the Wedgwood family, a common practice in Victorian upper-class families.

scenes.text: Wedgwood's anti-slavery medallion became one of the first great pieces of political merchandise — mass-produced, distributed widely, worn by abolitionists from London to Philadelphia. His grandson Charles Darwin would inherit his moral seriousness along with his scientific curiosity.

challenge.instruction: Wedgwood sells to queens and shopkeepers alike. Trade his china as royal orders, rivals and canal news move the price, and finish richer than you started.
challenge.fact: Wedgwood was a major investor in the Grand Trunk Canal, which connected his Staffordshire potteries to the ports at Liverpool and Hull. He understood that transport was as important as manufacturing — cheap bulk movement of clay in and finished goods out made his mass-production model possible.

scenes.speaker: Josiah Wedgwood
scenes.text: A craftsman makes one pot. A merchant sells one pot. But I have built a system — design, manufacturing, distribution, marketing — that will make ten million pots, each one beautiful, each one reaching a home that would never have afforded beauty before. That is what industry can be, at its best.

challenge.instruction: The system ends where the ware leaves Etruria: on the Trent and Mersey Canal. Work the boats up and down the narrow locks and waste as little of the scarce summit water as you can.
challenge.fact: Wedgwood brilliantly marketed at both ends of the market. He sold exclusive pieces to royalty and aristocracy — then used their endorsements to sell affordable versions to the growing middle class. His catalogue, free delivery, and money-back guarantee made quality ceramics accessible to ordinary households, pioneering the modern retail model.

scenes.speaker: Josiah Wedgwood
scenes.text: Two face-down cards: one at Boston, one at St Petersburg. We cannot see who they are until we attack, and an attack reveals every card at the location. The Business War already runs at Boston; you hold a card to start one at St Petersburg.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 5 · Face Down. Win two attacks: fight at Boston where the Business War is running, then carry the fight to St Petersburg by starting your own event there.
challenge.fact: A card on the board can be public (face up) or private (face down). A private card hides its identity and stats from rivals until an attack reveals every card at that location. Your own cards deploy face down; Toggle Public when being seen helps you.
